result:
If I could change the world in one way, it would be to eliminate the barriers that prevent people from accessing education, opportunity, and dignity—regardless of their background, identity, or circumstances. Education is the foundation for empathy, innovation, and equity, and when it’s truly accessible, it can dismantle cycles of poverty, discrimination, and violence.

But more than just access, I’d want to transform education into a system that nurtures curiosity, critical thinking, and creativity—not just rote memorization or rigid conformity. A world where every person feels valued, heard, and empowered to shape their own future would be one where progress isn’t just possible, but inevitable.

(And if I’m being selfish, I’d also make sure there’s unlimited coffee and fewer bugs. But the first part is more important.)
